blog.title: Food and Travel Guide: Discover Famous Local Dishes Around the World
blog.content:
Introduction

Travel is about more than visiting famous landmarks. One of the most rewarding ways to understand a destination is through its food. A local breakfast, a family-run restaurant or a traditional street-food market can reveal a great deal about a region's culture and everyday life.

A good food and travel guide helps you discover regional specialities, find authentic dining experiences and plan meals around your itinerary. Whether you are exploring India's diverse cuisines or travelling internationally, food can become one of the highlights of your journey.

Here are some famous dishes and destinations to consider when planning your next food-focused holiday.

1. Delhi, India – Chaat and Butter Chicken

Delhi is a rewarding destination for travellers who enjoy bold flavours and a mix of regional influences.

Popular choices include chaat, parathas, kebabs and butter chicken. Different neighbourhoods have their own food traditions, so exploring local eateries can be just as interesting as visiting the city's monuments.

Travel tip: Choose busy, well-maintained food establishments, check food hygiene and ask about spice levels before ordering.

You can explore sightseeing and food experiences through the official Delhi Tourism website.

2. Hyderabad, India – Hyderabadi Biryani

Hyderabad is famous for Hyderabadi biryani, a rice dish associated with aromatic spices and distinctive cooking methods. The city also offers haleem during particular seasons, along with kebabs and traditional sweets.

Travel tip: Compare different established restaurants and ask whether a dish is available in a particular style. Recipes and spice levels can vary from one kitchen to another.

3. Kolkata, India – Kathi Rolls and Sweets

Kolkata is well known for its street-food culture and sweets. Travellers often look for kathi rolls, puchka and traditional Bengali desserts.

The city's food scene provides a mix of quick snacks, historic eateries and regional dishes.

Travel tip: Plan a food walk with enough time between stops so you can enjoy smaller portions instead of ordering too much at once.

4. Jaipur, India – Dal Baati Churma

Jaipur offers a chance to explore the flavours of Rajasthan. Dal baati churma is a well-known traditional meal, while ghewar and other sweets are popular choices for visitors.

The city's markets and traditional restaurants can make a food-focused outing a natural addition to a sightseeing itinerary.

Travel tip: During hot weather, carry water and plan outdoor food walks for cooler parts of the day.

5. Mumbai, India – Vada Pav and Pav Bhaji

Mumbai's food culture includes quick street snacks, traditional Maharashtrian dishes and a wide variety of regional cuisines.

Vada pav and pav bhaji are among the city's best-known casual foods. Visitors can also discover seafood dishes and restaurants serving food from across India.

Travel tip: Select vendors with good food-handling practices and freshly prepared items. If you have allergies or dietary restrictions, communicate them clearly before ordering.

6. Naples, Italy – Neapolitan Pizza

Naples is widely associated with Neapolitan pizza, which traditionally features a soft, airy crust and simple toppings.

For food lovers, the city offers an opportunity to learn how local ingredients, cooking traditions and regional identity influence a dish that is now popular around the world.

Travel tip: Look for restaurants that specialise in the local style, and check opening times because some establishments close between service periods.

7. Tokyo, Japan – Sushi and Ramen

Tokyo is a major destination for travellers interested in Japanese cuisine. Options range from sushi and ramen to tempura, soba noodles and regional specialities.

Food experiences can vary from casual noodle shops to fine dining, making it possible to explore different styles within the same trip.

Travel tip: Research restaurant reservation requirements in advance, especially for popular or small establishments. Check ingredients carefully if you have allergies.

8. Bangkok, Thailand – Pad Thai and Tom Yum

Bangkok is known for its lively food markets and wide range of Thai dishes. Visitors often seek pad Thai, tom yum soup, curries and mango sticky rice.

Food stalls, local restaurants and contemporary dining venues offer different ways to explore the city's cuisine.

Travel tip: Ask for the spice level you prefer. If you have a sensitive stomach, start with freshly cooked food from vendors that maintain good hygiene.

9. Istanbul, Türkiye – Kebabs and Baklava

Istanbul's food culture reflects its position between Europe and Asia. Travellers can explore kebabs, pide, meze, simit and baklava, along with Turkish tea and coffee.

Markets and neighbourhood restaurants offer opportunities to sample traditional flavours while exploring the city's historic areas.

Travel tip: Check menu prices before ordering and confirm whether service charges are included.

10. Paris, France – Croissants and French Pastries

Paris is a favourite destination for travellers who enjoy bakeries, cafés and classic French cuisine. Croissants, baguettes, pastries and regional cheeses are among the familiar foods visitors may want to try.

A bakery stop can be an easy addition to a day spent exploring museums, gardens and historic streets.

Travel tip: Visit neighbourhood bakeries early for a wider selection, and consider exploring areas beyond the busiest tourist streets.

How to Plan a Food-Focused Trip

Research Local Specialities Before You Go

Make a short list of dishes associated with the destination. Researching regional foods helps you avoid spending the entire trip eating familiar international meals.

Explore Beyond Tourist Restaurants

Popular attractions often have restaurants aimed primarily at visitors. Explore residential neighbourhoods and established local eateries as well, while choosing places with good hygiene standards.

Balance Street Food and Restaurant Meals

Street food can be an affordable way to try local flavours, while sit-down restaurants may be better for dishes that require longer preparation. Choose based on the food, your budget and the hygiene standards you can observe.

Check Dietary Needs

If you follow a vegetarian or vegan diet, or have food allergies, learn the local words for your requirements. Ask about ingredients, cooking oils, sauces and cross-contact where relevant.

Build Meals Into Your Itinerary

Avoid scheduling every meal far away from your sightseeing route. Group food stops by neighbourhood to save time and enjoy a more relaxed trip.

Respect Local Food Customs

Some destinations have specific dining etiquette or customs around meals. Observe local practices and ask politely when you are unsure.

For further inspiration about regional Indian dishes, the National Portal of India’s culinary section is a useful starting point.

Food Travel on a Budget

You do not need an expensive restaurant budget to enjoy a destination's cuisine.

  • Try local breakfast dishes.

  • Compare menu prices before ordering.

  • Share larger dishes when appropriate.

  • Visit markets and food halls with clear hygiene standards.

  • Choose seasonal specialities.

  • Avoid ordering more than you can comfortably eat.

  • Keep some flexibility in your daily food budget.

A combination of casual meals and one or two special dining experiences can make a trip both memorable and affordable.

Food Safety While Travelling

Trying local cuisine should be enjoyable, but basic precautions matter.

Choose freshly cooked food from establishments that handle ingredients safely. Wash or sanitise your hands before eating, drink safe water and be cautious with food that has been left exposed for long periods.

Travellers with allergies or medical dietary requirements should take additional precautions and carry any necessary medication according to their healthcare professional's advice.

Final Thoughts

A food and travel experience offers more than a list of famous dishes. It gives you a chance to learn about regional traditions, meet local people and discover how food connects with a destination's history and daily life.

From biryani in Hyderabad to pizza in Naples and ramen in Tokyo, each place has something distinctive to offer. Plan thoughtfully, stay curious and choose food experiences that suit your preferences.

Explore more destination ideas and practical guides at Best Travel Advisory and make local cuisine part of your next adventure.

Food traditions vary by region, restaurant and season, so treat these dishes as starting points for exploration rather than a complete list of local specialities.
